pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in order.
test 'AC-3' checks only done items, ✓ prefix, id order (marks 3 then 1).
test 'AC-4' checks all items in order with ✓ only on done.
test 'AC-5' asserts exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty, __proto__ values; code uses Object.hasOwn.
test 'AC-7' covers empty table in all three views, Nothing open., Nothing done yet.
traffic/routes.json lists both; test 'AC-8' checks it.

findings.what: Commit 53c8e9b 'Follow-up edits' replaced `expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` with `.toBeDefined()`, which can never fail. The test 'on a due minute hits /healthz and every listed route' no longer checks which routes the traffic worker requests. This loosens an existing test with no spec justification, and the commit message hides it.
findings.fix: Restore the `toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` assertion. The fake app now records pathname+search, so it should pass.

findings.what: The PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened a traffic test to an always-true assertion. The body also describes the fake-app change as the only traffic-test change.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim accurate, or disclose the change.

findings.what: A table that is non-empty but where view=done or open is empty costs an extra COUNT query only in the empty case. This is fine, but the COUNT query has no test for a mixed state beyond the AC-7 sequence.

lenses.note: Spec present; decisions (open default, query parameter, GET-only) are followed.
All 8 ACs and all 6 state rows have tests. No spec edits after go.
The final commit weakened a traffic test to toBeDefined(). I did not run the test suite (it needs the Workers pool), and CI covers that.
The query is built from a fixed whitelist, so there is no injection. The traffic route check regex is relaxed to allow ?, which the spec's AC-8 requires.
The view value is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn and the titles are escaped. Nothing planted in the repo tries to steer the review.
Only a minimal server-rendered nav and list; no stylesheet or UI component files in the diff.
No browser flow was available; the diff has no UI framework files.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false for the final commit.
